atom_id: G01 Sigma_t search state (R4: what does 'nearby state' mean)
donor_source_ids: Kantorovich 1942; duality and metric properties of W_p (Villani 2009 survey form, already in HSG ledger as R4 OWNS for this atom's parents_hint)
donor_structure: Kantorovich/Wasserstein: W_c(mu, nu) = inf over couplings pi of E_pi[c(x,y)]; W_c is a metric on probability measures whenever c is a metric on the base space; duality gives a certificate (dual potentials) for optimality.
target_structure: a metric d on the HSG search state Sigma_t sufficient for R4 (metric geometry of search states: nearby states should mean 'cheap to reach / similar in behaviour').
mapping: base space -> elementary state transformations (edits/amendments); ground cost c -> burden of an elementary transformation; state distribution mu -> distribution over reachable states (or deterministic state as Dirac); search-state distance -> W_1 over transformation-cost structure; coupling -> joint plan moving one state to another.
preserved_relations: metric axioms: W_1 is a genuine metric iff ground cost is (directly inherited)
dual certificate: optimal transport plans carry potentials = 'witness of cheapest move' - reusable as reachability certificate (ties to G12 reach)
metrization of 'nearby': convergence in W_1 = weak convergence + convergence of ground-cost moments - a principled notion of state proximity
known_broken_relations: computability: for program-like states the ground cost (minimal edit burden between states) is only semicomputable in general (Rice-type obstruction via T15); the metric exists mathematically but is not uniformly computable - breaks the use of d for cache/licence decisions (G14 hostile H3 analog)

behavioural metric mismatch: W_1 over edit cost measures syntactic proximity; two syntactically distant states can be behaviourally identical (neutral sets, P1) - d is not a behavioural metric without quotienting by the garbling order (P2)
burden-plateau discontinuity inherits G10's LIFT_FAILS: burden is not Lipschitz in any cheap metric (hostile_burden_lipschitz.json H1)
unknown_correspondences: whether an admissible restricted ground-cost family (amendment grammar-restricted edits) restores computability is open - the natural candidate for an HSG residual theorem
interaction of W_1 with kernel contraction (Dobrushin delta) unmeasured
assumptions_added: elementary transformation set and its burden costs fixed by the constitution (vii)
states embedded in a space where the ground cost is defined (measurable edit space)
candidate_theorem: A search-state metric exists at R4 iff the elementary-transformation ground cost is itself a metric; admissibility (burden-Lipschitz, computable) fails in general and is restored only under grammar-restricted edit families.
strongest_parent: Kantorovich 1942 / Villani survey (metric property of W_c under metric ground cost; standard, ledger-verified for this atom)
route: L0 shortlist + L1 survey + L2 duality read + map/synth/validate; validation via counterexample attempt on computability and burden-Lipschitz (both succeed as obstructions -> conditional form)
status_rationale: parent owns the metric construction; the HSG-specific admissibility (computability, burden-Lipschitz) is obstructed in general - receipt delivers the conditional statement plus the named restricted-family escape, which is the genuinely new content.
